parole.significato: duvet, continental quilt, comforter (a padded cover for a bed)
parole.testo: First attested in c. 1395. From Byzantine Greek πάπλωμα (páplōma), from Ancient Greek πέπλος (péplos, “veil, sheet”).

parole.significato: rat (a medium-sized rodent belonging to the genus Rattus)
parole.testo: A wanderword. Via either Slovene podgána or Italian pantegana. Compare Venetan pantegàna (“rat”). Ultimately from Byzantine Greek ποντικός (pontikós), from μῦς ποντικός (mûs pontikós, “rat”, literally “pontic mouse”).

From either South Slavic or East Slavic, from Old Church Slavonic сѫбота (sǫbota), from Byzantine Greek *σάμβατον (*sámbaton), from Ancient Greek σάββατον (sábbaton), from Hebrew שַׁבָּת (šabbāṯ).
